pathway_name: Prebiotic photoredox synthesis followed by Strecker amino acid synthesis
description: A plausible abiotic synthesis of threonine from formaldehyde, hydrogen cyanide, hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, and water. Photochemical reactions produce lactaldehyde, which undergoes Strecker chemistry and hydrolysis to form threonine.

molecules.stereochemistry: Unspecified; abiotic synthesis can generate threonine and allo-threonine stereoisomers.

molecules.role: Formal oxidation product used for balancing the photoredox reactions

reactions.name: Formation of glycolonitrile
reactions.conditions: Aqueous environment containing formaldehyde and cyanide
reactions.description: Hydrogen cyanide adds to formaldehyde to form glycolonitrile.

reactions.name: Photoreduction of glycolonitrile
reactions.equation: HOCH2CN + H2S + H2O -> HOCH2CHO + NH3 + S
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation, copper(I) cyanide photoredox catalyst, aqueous sulfide and phosphate buffer
reactions.description: Reduction of the nitrile functionality produces glycolaldehyde. Hydrogen sulfide supplies reducing equivalents.
reactions.reported_yield: 42% glycolaldehyde after 2 hours under the reported laboratory conditions

reactions.name: Formation of acetaldehyde
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation, copper cyanide photoredox chemistry, sulfide and thiocyanate
reactions.description: The hydroxymethyl group of glycolaldehyde undergoes reductive deoxygenation, generating acetaldehyde.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally observed; conversion improved in the presence of thiocyanate

reactions.name: Formation of acetaldehyde cyanohydrin
reactions.description: Hydrogen cyanide adds to acetaldehyde to produce 2-hydroxypropanenitrile.

reactions.name: Formation of lactaldehyde
reactions.equation: CH3CH(OH)CN + H2S + H2O -> CH3CH(OH)CHO + NH3 + S
reactions.conditions: UV irradiation, copper(I) cyanide catalyst, aqueous hydrogen sulfide
reactions.description: Reduction of acetaldehyde cyanohydrin produces lactaldehyde, the required three-carbon aldehyde precursor of threonine.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally demonstrated by Ritson and Sutherland (2013)
reactions.reported_yield: 19% lactaldehyde after 2 hours in the reported experiment

reactions.name: Formation of lactaldehyde cyanohydrin
reactions.description: Addition of hydrogen cyanide to lactaldehyde forms 2,3-dihydroxybutanenitrile.
reactions.evidence: Supported by the experimentally studied prebiotic reaction sequence

reactions.name: Formation of threonine aminonitrile
reactions.conditions: Aqueous ammonia and cyanide; equilibration over days
reactions.description: Under Strecker reaction conditions, cyanohydrin and aldehyde-imine equilibria allow the formation of 2-amino-3-hydroxybutanenitrile. The equation represents the net transformation rather than a direct substitution mechanism.
reactions.evidence: Experimentally demonstrated formation of the threonine/allo-threonine aminonitrile precursor

reactions.name: Partial hydrolysis to threoninamide
reactions.conditions: Aqueous hydrolysis, potentially promoted by acid, base, or heating
reactions.description: Hydrolysis of the nitrile group produces the corresponding amino acid amide.
reactions.evidence: Established nitrile hydrolysis chemistry; this particular step is proposed for the prebiotic network

reactions.name: Formation of threonine
reactions.conditions: Aqueous hydrolysis, potentially promoted by acid, base, or heating
reactions.description: Hydrolysis of the amide group generates 2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid (threonine).
reactions.evidence: Established amide hydrolysis chemistry; the complete prebiotic sequence has not been demonstrated as a single experiment

pathway_summary.prebiotic_environment: UV-irradiated aqueous environments containing cyanide, sulfide, and copper minerals, followed by conditions favorable to nitrile and amide hydrolysis.
pathway_summary.stereochemical_limitations: The proposed abiotic reactions are not intrinsically selective for biologically relevant L-threonine. Threonine, allo-threonine, and their enantiomers may be produced.
pathway_summary.scientific_limitations: The photoredox generation of lactaldehyde and its conversion to an aminonitrile have experimental support. Hydrolysis to threonine is chemically established in the general Strecker framework, but the uninterrupted full prebiotic sequence has not been experimentally verified. Elemental sulfur in the balanced redox equations represents formal sulfur oxidation bookkeeping; actual sulfur-containing products can differ.

references.authors: Ritson, D. J. and Sutherland, J. D.
references.title: Synthesis of Aldehydic Ribonucleotide and Amino Acid Precursors by Photoredox Chemistry
references.relevance: Primary experimental evidence for production of glycolaldehyde, acetaldehyde, lactaldehyde, and threonine aminonitrile precursors.

references.title: Interstellar formation of lactaldehyde, a key intermediate in the methylglyoxal pathway
references.relevance: Independent evidence for abiotic lactaldehyde production and its relevance to prebiotic threonine chemistry.

references.title: Proton transfers in the Strecker reaction revealed by DFT calculations
references.relevance: Mechanistic support for aminonitrile formation and hydrolysis to amino acids.
